clue.text: Rich lawman taking on financial commitments

parts.note: cop is slang for a police officer
IOUs are written promises to repay debts

explanation.surface: A wealthy police officer has started taking on debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rich' here means plentiful, as in a rich harvest, not wealthy; 'taking on' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Copious means abundant, and rich can mean plentiful or abundant.

clue.text: Well-liked musical instrument —- a single note shows nothing can touch it!

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable, as in 'the in crowd'
a viola is a stringed instrument slightly larger than a violin
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that a popular viola and one note make an untouchable performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inviolate is kept safe from harm or violation: untouchable.

clue.text: People mature in a commune

parts.note: men can mean people in general, or a group of workers
to age is to grow older or mature

explanation.surface: People growing older together in a hippy commune.
explanation.definitionFit: A ménage is a household, a group living together, much like a small commune.

clue.text: Flora and fauna fill wide compounds

indicators.note: to compound is to mix together, so the letters are combined into a new order

explanation.surface: Plants and animals fill wide enclosures.
explanation.definitionFit: Wildlife is the collective term for wild plants and animals of a region.

clue.text: Meteorologists —- could be two, perhaps three

definitions.text: Meteorologists —- could be two, perhaps three

parts.words: Meteorologists —- could be two, perhaps three
parts.note: the hedged guess 'could be two, perhaps three' is the sort of uncertain forecast the people who predict sunshine and showers are teased for making

explanation.surface: Forecasters hedge about how many degrees or inches to expect.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteorologists forecast conditions, so they are jokingly seers of rain and shine.

clue.text: Cutting fruit as not drinking, but that will not happen again!

indicators.note: the words 'as not drinking' cut into the fruit, splitting it open

parts.note: a lime is a green citrus fruit
TT means teetotal, abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: Someone slicing citrus vows never to drink again.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying it is the last time is a promise that something will never be repeated.

clue.text: A course set with little hesitation

parts.note: to lay a table is to set it
er is the short sound people make when hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone sets a dinner course down with a slight pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' is a row of bricks or stones in a wall, not a part of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: In building, a course is a single horizontal row or level of bricks.

clue.text: Pro, having a pain in the neck, held back

parts.note: pro means in favour of, as does for
a bore is a tiresome, irritating person or thing

explanation.surface: A professional suffering a stiff neck held back from playing.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbear is to refrain, and its past tense describes having restrained oneself.

clue.text: Start battling with weight in spring

indicators.note: the start of the word battling is its opening letter

parts.note: an ounce is a small imperial unit of weight

explanation.surface: A boxer starts fighting in spring with a weight division.
explanation.definitionFit: Bounce and spring both mean resilience or a leap upwards.

clue.text: They are analytical, like a detective-story writer

parts.note: as means in the manner of, like
Dorothy L. Sayers wrote the Lord Peter Wimsey detective novels

explanation.surface: Analysts compared with a crime novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Assayers test metals and ores to analyse their composition.

clue.text: Set new limit and a conservationist body will be up in arms

indicators.note: the word limit is set out in a new order

parts.note: NT is the National Trust, the British charity that conserves historic houses and land

explanation.surface: A heritage charity sets a new limit and members rise in protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Militant means aggressively combative, ready to take up arms or protest.

clue.text: A sailing man with no money backing a big fish

parts.note: tar is an old term for a sailor

indicators.note: backing means the words 'no money' are read in reverse order

parts.note: p stands for penny or pence

explanation.surface: A penniless sailor dreams of landing a big fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarpon is a large silvery game fish of warm Atlantic waters.

clue.text: A light centrally placed?

parts.note: a thick round glass lens in a lantern, ship or roof, and also the centre of a dartboard or target

explanation.surface: Where to place a lamp in a room.
explanation.definitionFit: A bull's-eye lantern has a bulging lens, and the term also names the very centre of a target.

clue.text: Prompter dealing with the baby-sitter

parts.note: re means concerning or about
a minder is someone who looks after children

explanation.surface: A note about the childminder.
explanation.definitionFit: A prompt is something that jogs the memory, which is what a memo or nudge does.

clue.text: Telling Iran grant is to be arranged

indicators.note: arranged signals that the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Reporting that a grant to Iran is pending.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling a story and recounting it are the same act.

clue.text: An end to double-parking accepted by the wise

indicators.note: the words being accepted are taken inside the other word

parts.note: a sage is a wise person

indicators.note: double means the letter for parking appears twice

parts.note: P is the map and road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Wise heads tolerate double-parking until it is stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'An end', so 'to' is a piece of the wordplay, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage is a halt or cessation of work or flow.

clue.text: He really doesn't like taking an animal without a checkup

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the animal goes around the other piece

parts.note: deer are hoofed animals
a test is an examination or checkup

explanation.surface: A man who hates taking his pet without a vet's checkup.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who loathes something hates it intensely.

clue.text: A man withdrawn before receiving discharge

indicators.note: the first piece receives the second, holding it inside

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before
to emit is to give off or discharge

explanation.surface: A man retreats before his wound starts oozing.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a hermit, a recluse who lives withdrawn from society.

clue.text: Maybe tries holding on, getting ever less able to pay

definitions.text: getting ever less able to pay

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the other word inside them
maybe signals that tries is only one possible ordering of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone tries to hold on while sinking deeper into debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' scrambles TRIES into STIER, and 'holding' puts ON inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stony-broke means penniless, so stonier is more short of cash.

clue.text: A redoubt, properly constructed, proves impossible to conquer

indicators.note: constructed signals the letters are built into a new order

explanation.surface: A well-built fortress is impregnable.
explanation.definitionFit: Obdurate means stubbornly unyielding, refusing to be moved or won over.

clue.text: Copy in large measure

definitions.meaning: a twice-normal serving of spirits in a bar

explanation.definitionFit: A duplicate of something is its twin, and a bar serving of spirits at twice the standard amount has the same name.

clue.text: Rises to fetch a little drink

parts.note: to fetch something is to get it
a sup is a small mouthful of drink

explanation.surface: Someone stands up to go and get a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise from bed or a seat is to stand.

clue.text: Scorch round the motorway and mark results

indicators.note: round means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: to sear is to scorch
M is used for motorway in British road names like the M1

explanation.surface: A car fire on the motorway leaves scorch marks.
explanation.definitionFit: A smear is a smudge or stain on a surface.

clue.text: Hanging around some rich aunt in great hopes of inheriting

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: A nephew lingers near a wealthy aunt, hoping for an inheritance.
explanation.definitionFit: Haunting a place means lingering about it frequently.

clue.text: The Left recapitulate, being well-informed

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
to iterate is to repeat or restate

explanation.surface: Left-wing politicians summarise their argument, showing they know their stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Literate can mean knowledgeable or educated in a field.

clue.text: Ways to incorporate cold cuts

indicators.note: the first word incorporates, or takes in, the other

parts.note: lanes are narrow roads or ways
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Methods of including cold meats on a platter.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor lances a boil by cutting it open.

clue.text: The sovereign is held by a noble lady to be beyond compare

indicators.note: the first words are held inside the noble lady

parts.note: a peeress is a woman holding a title in the peerage
a sovereign is a gold coin worth one pound, and L is the abbreviation for pound (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: A monarch is embraced by a titled lady who is unrivalled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The sovereign' looks like the monarch (ER) but is the coin: a pound, L.
explanation.definitionFit: Peerless means without equal, unmatched.
